mechanism_narrative: Tightening restrictions drive a sharp drop in WORKPLACES mobility, which precedes a decline in retail-and-recreation footfall because commuter and office-based trips are cut first. As workplaces stay below -30% for the next four weeks, RETAIL_REC will fall further.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from -34.0 at t-3w to -45.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains below -30% for four weeks but the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility is a leading indicator of retail-and-recreation because both depend on discretionary trips. The recent 10.9-point drop in TRANSIT to -47.0% signals a persistent decline in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -36.1 at t-1w to -47.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is below -40% but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than its t-0w level, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility exceeds 15% above baseline, households are staying home in a sustained way, reducing non-essential retail trips. The current 17.9% reading triggers a further decline in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean exceeds 15% above baseline
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL is above 15% but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Falling grocery-and-pharmacy and parks mobility jointly signal a broad contraction in out-of-home activity. With GROCERY_PHARM turning negative and PARKS dropping below -40%, RETAIL_REC will decline over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell to -5.3 and PARKS to -41.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM is negative and PARKS is below -40% but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A seasonal winter decline in parks usage reduces overall outdoor and adjacent retail activity. When PARKS falls below -30% for two consecutive weeks, retail-and-recreation footfall follows downward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -30% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -15.1 at t-3w to -41.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below -30% for two weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last 28-day mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sharp declines in workplaces and transit indicate new or intensified restrictions. When both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are below -40%, the retail sector contracts further over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES < -40 and TRANSIT < -40 in the same week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both below -40% but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Extreme drops in retail, transit, and workplaces may exhaust the downside, causing adaptation and a short-term rebound. With RETAIL_REC below -30% and TRANSIT below -40%, retail-and-recreation mobility rises over the next week.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC is below -30% and TRANSIT is below -40% but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its t-0w value, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A negative reading in grocery-and-pharmacy mobility indicates that even essential shopping trips are contracting. This broad consumer pullback drags retail-and-recreation down over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 3.1 at t-3w to -5.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains negative but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its last 28-day mean, the hypothesis fails.
